text:
I needed to have a wisdom tooth extracted. I read the reviews of all the dental clinics. There was one for this place that I trusted.
The bad reviews made me wary, but they were about poor service. My experience was great! Everyone was very kind! At all times!
There are several steps to follow upon arrival, which might be confusing. But it's super easy, and many people speak English. If you have trouble, I recommend using your phone's translator. Also, read the directions to the places to go upon arrival, which are in one of the comments.
First, you have to go to reception and fill out a form, then go to another area, then to the dentist who will evaluate you. If you need to have the tooth extracted or go to another area, they will tell you.
If you have to go to area 3, which is for the tooth extraction, when you arrive, you have to open the window and leave the pink slip of paper in the basket, and they will call you later. This is important because you might arrive at department 3 and sit and wait, and they never call you. Remember, if you have any questions, ask; everyone is very kind and will help you.
Then a student will attend to you and extract the tooth. If they have any complications, they'll call the professor.
You pay when you leave.
I had asked how much it would cost beforehand, and they charged me what they told me: 4 euros.
They explained the ENTIRE procedure to me at ALL times.
I got very nervous and cried from fear before starting, and the student who attended to me held my hand, calmed me down, and told me that we wouldn't start until I felt ready, that she would wait as long as I needed, and not to worry, that she was there for me. She was an angel. Very professional. When they finished, they gave me gauze.

I'm very grateful.
It's important to understand that this is a faculty where you're seen by students supervised by professors, so obviously it's not the same as going to a specialist. There's a risk that something might go wrong, but there are very professional professors, and the price is very affordable. Everything was incredibly quick and painless, and everyone was so kind.
Dentists in Thailand are highly professional! And everything is very hygienic.
My congratulations to the student and professor who treated me, as well as the reception staff and all the other personnel!

text:
I can directly compare my experience at this facility with expensive UK private healthcare for the same issue, and this place was so much more efficient, it's scary.

I had a rare abscess in the root of a tooth, it had been developing for about a year and was just getting bigger and bigger. I went to a regular dentist in CM, who referred me here. It took about 3-4 hours for me to get assessed, referred to various departments, x-rayed, and presented with treatment options.

I chose the surgical option but was told I would have to wait 3 weeks for the surgery. I was due to visit home in the UK in 3 weeks, so I decided I would get it done in the UK when I went back.

I made an appointment with my UK dentist for the day after I arrived in the UK. He referred me to a specialist, that was about a 6-week wait (and this is private healthcare, NHS probably would have taken a year). The specialist didn't need to take x-rays, because I brought my CT scan from CMU Dental Faculty, if I didn't have it, that would have been another referral and more weeks/months waiting.

The UK specialist (a renowned facial reconstructive surgeon, it turned out), gave me the EXACT treatment options I received at CMU Dental Faculty. Again, I choose the surgical option. The wait for surgery was another 6-8 weeks.

If I had done the entire thing in the UK, it would have taken about 4 months to get to the same stage it took 4 hours to get to at CMU Dental Faculty. Then the wait for surgery was more than double.

My surgery in the UK went amazingly, my Doctor was one of the best facial surgeons in the world, so I'm very happy with the outcome.

But I don't understand how UK healthcare can't move as fast as it does here.

Everyone I saw at CMU Dental Faculty was knowledgeable and able to explain to me what was going on and what my options were. I felt in good hands all the way.
